sharedNumericGuard.constraint: These guards explicitly cover new pane-context contracts, not every existing wire declaration. A Double conversion in guarded paths is not evidence that arbitrary UInt64 values are permitted or rounded.
sharedNumericGuard.aboveBoundFailure: IPCPaneNumericEncodingError maps internalError -32603; representative adapters also call requireSafe before result formation.
sharedNumericGuard.failureCaveat: The direct numeric error mapper is not every encoding failure route: IPCMethodContract.encodedValue catches JSONEncoder errors and wraps them as IPCSchemaValidationError.decodingMismatch. Representative adapters guard counters before typed result formation. No uniform failure code is inferred for all untraced nested encoders.

presenceCases.currentOutcome: Both generic decodeResponse and discovery header reject: hasResult=false and hasError=false.

Generic decodeIfPresent yields nil; discovery contains+decodeNil sets hasResult=false; both reject. Public success(.null) can be composed by encoder API, but these readers do not accept it as a sole success result. Source counterexample, not demonstrated production incident.
Both reject by exclusive nonnil-value check. This is not strict XOR on key existence.

counterexamplesAndRisks.claim: All responses use JSONValue is too broad: cached command.list/system.capabilities plus explicit client discovery retain encoded result Data across their respective boundaries.
Handler/descriptor returning encoded Data does not imply raw result end-to-end: ordinary registration decodes it to JSONValue and ordinary CLI reparses/re-encodes result before normalization.
UInt64 field declarations do not imply full UInt64 wire range. Representative pane epoch/positions/revision/stale write numbers have explicit safe-bound encode/decode/schema checks.

All staleness is an error is too broad: lastAccepted is current typed success stale result. Current searched explicit staleness-error producers carry writerReplaced; generic error mapping can encode enum but CLI failure projection does not preserve arbitrary staleness payload.
Initial subscription result and later notification are different routes. Notification client performs generic validation but forwards original String; it does not normalize parsed event into output.

Unchecked numeric domains in other/untraced contracts would need their own range/production-route evidence before precision equivalence could be claimed. No measured rounding or confirmed current precision incident follows from these declarations.
Envelope explicit-null result is treated as absent by both response readers; some nested optional fields accept/collapse/omit null. Current behavior is not one universal null-preservation rule.
